1952 still etched on his memory
2017-02-26T00:00:00+06:00 | Our Correspondent, Mymensingh
https://www.thedailystar.net/country/1952-still-etched-his-memory-1367233

Too feeble to speak and walk, Khandakar Abdul Malek Shahidullah still narrates the days of his participation in Language Movement in heroic mood.

“I was a Class IX student then and when the wave of Language Movement accelerated in Mymensingh region in 1952, I along with other schoolboys brought out processions protesting the move,” said the 82-year-old language hero.

A former member of the provincial assembly, Shahidullah hails from Nandibari area in Muktagachha upazila.

Recalling the days of 1952, the language movement veteran said “I along with eight students of Cooperative High School was expelled for joining the movement, but all except me, got back their studentship seeking apology.”

“My medical officer father did not allow me to apologise, and eventually my education life stopped for ever”, he said.

Shahidullah, also an organiser of the Liberation War, was the organising secretary of Awami League in grater Mymensingh when Shaheed Syed Nazrul Islam was its president.

Now the Language Movement veteran is suffering from various old age complications, including respiratory disease, said family members.

Advocate Emdadul Haque Millat, president of Communist Party of Bangladesh in Mymensingh, said Shahidullah deserves 'Ekushey Padak' for his contribution in the Language Movement.
